CHIEF COMPLAINT
Pain at the end of right middle finger.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
41-year-old female presents with 4-5 days of right middle finger pain following a motor vehicle accident. Patient was stopped at a four-way stop when she was rear-ended by another vehicle. She became angry and attempted to flip off the other driver but was overly enthusiastic with the gesture and struck the ceiling of her car with her right middle finger. The accident resulted in minor damage to the vehicle (crumpled trunk). Patient denies any other injuries from the accident.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atrial fibrillation.

MEDICATIONS
Digoxin.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Exam is normal other than tenderness over the distal phalanx of the right middle finger. Palpation over the distal phalanx elicits pain. No tenderness with palpation lower down the finger.

RESULTS
X-ray shows distal phalanx fracture of the right middle finger.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Distal phalanx fracture of the right middle finger. Tramadol 50 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain, 8 tablets dispensed. Finger splint placed. Follow-up x-ray in two weeks.
